facts.label: official
facts.quote: The co-operative bank was also holding substantial amount (` 800.00 crore) of inter-bank deposits from a large number of UCBs in Gujarat and from other banks and this posed a systemic risk for the co-operative banks in Gujarat.
facts.text: Madhavpura Mercantile Co-operative Bank held Rs 800.00 crore in inter-bank deposits from numerous urban cooperative banks in Gujarat and other institutions when it faced a bank run.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: By a detailed order dated 12.12.2003 passed by the Board they were all debarred from associating with the securities market for a period of 14 years.
facts.text: The Securities Appellate Tribunal upheld an order debarring Ketan Parekh and his associated entities from associating with the securities market for a period of 14 years.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The MMCB had issued pay orders worth ₹1,200 crore (US$120 million) to stock broker Ketan Parekh, which he discounted at Bank of India.
facts.text: Madhavpura Mercantile Co-operative Bank had issued pay orders worth Rs 1,200 crore to stockbroker Ketan Parekh prior to the market crash.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: At the time banks in India were not allowed to lend more than ₹15 crore (US$1.6 million) to stock brokers.
facts.text: Under prevailing banking regulations during the 2001 scam, Indian banks were prohibited from lending more than Rs 15 crore to stock brokers.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: In 1999–2000, when the bank had 50,000 public depositors, it started lending out large sums of money to stock brokers in gross violation of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules and regulations.
facts.text: Madhavpura Mercantile Co-operative Bank had 50,000 public depositors when it started illegally diverting large sums to stock broking entities.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: however, when the dotcom bubble burst, the Sensex dropped down to 3,000 points, and Parekh and the bank started having problems.
facts.text: The benchmark Sensex fell sharply to 3,000 points following the dot-com bubble collapse, leading to unpaid pay orders and the freezing of bank liquidity.

facts.text: When the cooperative bank collapse happened in 2001, household savings deposits were insured only up to a maximum limit of Rs 1,00,000 per depositor under DICGC guidelines.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Deposit insurance cover increased from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh with effect from February 4, 2020.
facts.text: To strengthen protection for retail households storing savings in commercial and cooperative banks, deposit insurance cover was increased to Rs 5,00,000 per depositor from February 4, 2020.
